paragraphs: 1. When Eli Pariser first encountered the internet, what did he think it was going to do?
a. The internet was going to show people the world.
b. The internet was going to make society better.
c. The internet was going to connect people.
d. The internet was going to do all of the above.
e. The internet was going to do none of the above.
2. What does Pariser say has changed about the internet?
a. He says the internet is less democratic.
b. Pariser says that the internet gives people more choices.
c. Pariser says that Facebook deletes information he doesn’t need.
d. Pariser describes a change in the way that information flows online.
3. What happened to the “conservatives” on Pariser’s Facebook page?
a. The conservatives began to disagree more often with Pariser’s ideas.
b. The conservatives “disappeared” from his Facebook page.
c. The conservatives stopped “liking” Pariser’s Facebook page.
d. Nothing happened to the conservatives on Pariser’s Facebook page.
4. Which of the following does Pariser NOT claim that Google monitors to influence the query results?
a. What kind of computer you use.
b. Which internet browser you are using.
c. Your location.
d. Your income.
e. Google monitors ALL of the above.
f. Google monitors NONE of the above.
5. Pariser says that there is something very important that we cannot see. What is it?
a. He says that we cannot see the things internet companies are monitoring.
b. He says that we cannot see internet companies tailoring our search results.
c. He says that we cannot see other people’s search results.
d. He says all of the above.
e. He says none of the above.
6. According to Pariser, what does the internet do today?
a. It maximizes profit by tailoring our internet experience.
b. It works more efficiently because it shows us what we are looking for.
c. The internet makes us smarter by exposing us to new ideas.
d. The internet shows us what it thinks we want to see.
7. According to Pariser, what is a filter bubble?
a. A bubble is our own, unique online experience.
b. A filter bubble is algorithm that decides what people experience when they go online.
c. The filter bubble is the information that people are missing when they go online.
d. Filter bubbles are problems in the system that allow unfriendly information to penetrate people’s queries.
8. According to Pariser, what important inner struggle does the internet take advantage of?
a. There is a struggle to control what we experience on the internet.
b. There is a struggle to decide which video we want to watch.
c. There is a struggle between what we think is good and what we find enjoyable.
d. There is competition between what we need to do and what we want to do.
e. People have difficulty choosing which link to click on.
f. Pariser cites ALL of the above as important inner struggles.
g. Parison cites NONE of the above as important inner struggles.
9. What do algorithmic gatekeepers pay attention to?
a. Pariser says that the gatekeepers notice what you click on first.
b. According to Pariser, the gatekeepers see everything that you do online.
c. The gatekeepers are programed to feed you information according to your needs.
d. The gatekeepers are designed to test your interests by offering you a variety of choices,
10. Pariser states that algorithmic gatekeepers lack what?
a. Judgement.
b. Empathy.
c. Ethics.
d. ALL of the above.
e. Pariser does not state that the gatekeepers lack any of the above.
11. Pariser says that the internet should NOT focus on what quality of information?
a. Important information.
b. Information that makes us uncomfortable.
c. Information that challenges us.
d. Relevant information.
e. Pariser says that the internet should show us ALL of the above.
f. Pariser says that the internet should not show us any of the above.
12. Which statement best describes Pariser’s view of journalistic ethics?
a. Journalistic ethics are a matter of personal choice.
b. Journalistic ethics are necessary for the flow of information.
c. Journalistic ethics prevent people from connecting.
d. Journalistic ethics are essential for a healthy society.
13. How many different behaviors does Google watch when we surf the web?
a. Google watches three primary behaviors.
b. Google watches thirteen of our behaviors.
c. Google looks for fifty-seven different behaviors.
d. Google watches all of our behaviors.
14. According to the video, what does Eli Parsier do for a living?
a. He is a software engineer.
b. He is a researcher in AI.
c. He is an author and activist.
d. He is all of the above.
e. The video does not say what Parsier does for a living.
15. Mark Zuckerberg reportedly said that “A squirrel dying in front of your house may be more relevant to your
interests right now than people dying in Africa.” Eli Parsier does NOT say, but IMPLIES, something
important about Zuckerberg’s statement. Which of the following best describes Parsier’s feelings?
a. People care more about things close to home than they care about things far away from their homes.
b. People care more about things they can change than things they cannot change.
c. People are more important than squirrels.
d. People will care about what internet gatekeepers put in front of them.
16. Which of the following does Eli Parsier NOT say we need the internet to do?
a. Find information faster.
b. Connect us to people.
c. Give us new ideas.
d. Expose us to different perspectives.
f. Parsier does not recommend that the internet do any of the above.
g. Parsier recommends that internet do ALL of the above.
